subject: Turkey
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about Istanbul. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). The Bosphorus is too narrow for the pinned map data to show reliably, so the city is a labelled approximate point.

claims.text: Istanbul is a city on two continents; about two-thirds of its population live in Europe and the rest in Asia.
Istanbul straddles the Bosphorus, one of the world’s busiest waterways, in northwestern Turkey.
With a population of over 15 million, Istanbul is home to 18% of the population of Turkey.
Istanbul’s position holds the only sea route between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean.
The lines on the European and Asian sides of the city are connected by the Marmaray Tunnel under the Bosphorus strait.
